title: Firms Switch Top AI Providers at Record 8% Rate in September
summary:
Management of corporate software budgets showed a trend of rapid provider turnover for artificial intelligence models during the third quarter. Spend management platform Ramp found that nearly 8% of businesses switched their primary model provider in September, the highest monthly rate the company has ever tracked on a three-month moving average. This turnover is driven by OpenAI's price cuts and a rapid cycle of new model releases, which are stripping pricing power from AI developers as services become commoditized.

The last comparable spike in switching occurred in May 2025 following the launch of Anthropic's Opus 4 and Sonnet 4. This volatility indicates that annual recurring revenue (ARR) is an unreliable metric for measuring AI expenditures due to a lack of long-term retention, suggesting that profit margins for AI labs will continue to decline.

Firms are switching AI providers at the highest rate Ramp has seen.

The monthly share of businesses switching their top model provider reached nearly 8% in September, measured as a three-month moving average. 

We last saw comparable switching when Anthropic launched Opus 4 and Sonnet 4 in May 2025.

Rapid model releases and OpenAI’s price cuts are giving firms reasons to switch. The more willing and able firms are to switch, the less pricing power AI labs have.

Another sign that AI models may be becoming commodities.
